subject: Geo-boundary architecture review — final scheduling options
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Müller <anya.mueller@continental-retail.com>, Satoshi Yamada <s.yamada@apac-retail.jp>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Geo-boundary architecture review — proposed slots

Hi Anya, Satoshi —

Thanks again for the interest in a technical deep-dive on deployment options across EU / US / APAC. We put together a short draft (redwood-arch-draft.pdf) that sketches options for data zoning, routing fallbacks, and KV-cache placement. Would love to run through the architecture with your infra and compliance teams and lock in next steps.

Proposed slots (all times local to the region listed):
- Option A: Tue 12 Oct — 09:00 PDT / 18:00 CEST / 01:00 JST (tight for APAC)
- Option B: Tue 12 Oct — 14:00 CEST / 05:00 PDT / 22:00 JST (APAC friendly)
- Option C: Wed 13 Oct — 08:00 PDT / 17:00 CEST / 00:00 JST (early APAC)

Agenda (30–45m):
- 5m: brief intro + goals
- 20m: architecture walk (routing, residency, fallback policies) — Evelyn
- 15m: kernel selection, batching, performance trade-offs — Jonas
- 10m: compliance ask + next steps — Karthik

Attachments: redwood-arch-draft.pdf (architectural sketch), redwood-residency-map.xlsx (region mapping).

Could you confirm which slot works, or suggest 2 alternatives? If preferred, we can split into a 40m arch review + 30m compliance appendix.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0186

Subject: Re: Geo-boundary architecture review — proposed slots

Thanks Ben — appreciate the options and the draft. Quick notes:

- Option A is tough for our EU infra team (late in their day) and impossible for our APAC folks.
- Option B (Tue 12 Oct, 14:00 CEST) looks promising — that hits late afternoon for us and should be manageable for APAC (Satoshi will join remotely).
- We do have a few specific asks for the call:
  - A short mapping of where PII vs. non-PII would be stored under each topology (high level is fine).
  - Any SOC2 / audit evidence we can look at ahead of time — our procurement team will want that.

Also, can you confirm whether the session will include a walkthrough of fallback behavior if a region gets full (e.g., routing to warm Dedicated or lower-cost variant)? That’s a critical design point for our operations team.

I’ll tentatively hold Tue 12 Oct 14:00 CEST — please send a calendar invite.

Best,
Anya Müller
Head of Cloud Operations | Continental Retail Group
anya.mueller@continental-retail.com

Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 11:20:00 -0700

Nice — thanks Anya for the quick reply and for tentatively holding Tue 12 Oct 14:00 CEST. A couple of clarifications from our side before we lock:

1) Split session: I agree with Ben that we can make the main review ~45m and then have a 20–30m compliance appendix for procurement/security questions. That keeps the core technical audience focused.

2) PII mapping: we've attached a simple residency spreadsheet (redwood-residency-map.xlsx) that maps data classes to suggested storage zones. During the call we can show the access controls and encryption boundary (KMIP/HSM integration notes).

3) Fallbacks: yes — Evelyn will show our routing policy prototype. In short: preference order is local-hosted -> dedicated pool in same region -> prefer warm capacity in a neighboring region (configured per-route) -> low-cost variant (quantized) as last resort. We'll have a short diagram and a failure-mode timeline to show.

4) Prep ask: can you share the list of teams that will join from your side (infra, procurement, security)? This will help us tailor slides.

I’m also attaching a small timezone grid (timezone-conversion.ics) that we can include in the invite so all participants see the local time.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
